text:
Hendrix Lapierre's family showed up in penguin costumes to watch him play for Pittsburgh, NHL.com reported. That's the most charming storyline of the month, and the hockey has been good too. After coming over from Washington in a trade for a third- and a fifth-round pick, he's playing 12:13 a night, up from 8:50 last season, and has 7 points in 13 games.

That's 0.54 points a game against 0.22 last season. Thirteen games is a small sample, and his points rate of 2.65 per 60 minutes is above the range we'd trust (1.4 to 2.3). Ice time settles faster than scoring does, and the ice time is the real gain here.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season found a signature: 22% of his setups go across the royal road, the side-to-side pass that moves a goalie, against 7% for a typical forward. That's the kind of skill that plays up when a player gets better linemates. He's 24, a 2020 first-round pick, and finally has room. We project about 32 points. If he holds his minutes through December, this trade will look like a steal for Pittsburgh.
headline: Lapierre gets a real chance
